headline: Approved decisions with changes for Harrison Road and Lafayette Street projects; continued Walmart Depot project at 440 Highland Avenue to September 3, 2026.
summary: The meeting covered several projects, including a housing and shelter project at Margin Street and Endicott Street. That project was referred to the Design Review Board. Members also approved decisions for the Harrison Road and Lafayette Street projects, and continued the 440 Highland Avenue project.
decisions: Referred the 56 Margin Street, 54 Margin Street, 7 High Street, 20 Endicott Street, and 24 Endicott Street project to the Design Review Board, 8-0 roll call vote.
Approved the decision with changes for 8 Harrison Road, 9 Harrison Road, 262 Loring Ave, and 266 Loring Ave, 7-0 roll call vote.
Approved the decision with changes for 73 Lafayette Street and related Lafayette Street, Derby Street, and Peabody Street parcels, 7-0 roll call vote with one recusal.
Continued the 440 Highland Avenue project to the September 3, 2026, regular Planning Board meeting, 9-0 roll call vote.
Approved the draft minutes from the July 9, 2026 regular meeting, 8-0 roll call vote with one present vote.

decision_evidence.quote: A motion to refer the project to the Design Review Board is made by Helen Sides, seconded by Sarah Tarbet and passes 8-0 in a roll call vote.
A motion to approve the decision with changes is made by Tom Furey, seconded by Jonathan Berk, and passes 7-0 in a roll call vote.
A motion to approve the decision with changes is made by Tom Furey, seconded by Helen Sides, and passes 7-0 with one recusal.
A motion to continue to the September 3, 2026, regular Planning Board meeting is made by Jonathan Berk, seconded by Helen Side, and passes 9-0 in a roll call vote.

A motion to approve the draft minutes from the July 9 2026, regular Planning Board meeting is made by Josh Turiel, seconded by Graham Wing, and passes 8-0 in a roll call vote, with one vote of “present.”

JOINT MEETING WITH THE DESIGN REVIEW BOARD MEETING AGENDA 
 
A joint public hearing of the Salem Planning Board and the Design Review Board was held on   
Thursday, July 23, 2026, at 6:30 p.m. via remote access. Public participation was possible   
via Zoom video and conference call.  
  
Chair Kirt Rieder calls the meeting to order at 6:32 p.m.  
 
Chair Rieder introduces Elena Eimert as a new Planning Board member and gives thanks to 
Carole Hamilton for her help and her many years of service. Ms. Chiancola echoes what Mr. 
Rieder said and states that the Mayor has awarded Ms. Hamilton a City Seal. Mr. Furey echoes 
the preceding words.

II. AGENDA 
A. 56 Margin Street, 54 Margin Street, 7 High Street, 20 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 
597), 24 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 595)  
Applicant: Harborlight Homes and Lifebridge North Shore  
Description: A continuance of a public hearing for all persons interested in the 
application of Harborlight Homes and Lifebridge North Shore at 56, 54 Margin 
Street, 20 Endicott Street, 7 High Street (Map 25, Lot 597) and 24 Endicott Street 
(Map 25, Lot 595) in the Residential Two-Family District (R2), Coastal Resilience 
Overlay District (C-ROD), Flood Hazard Overlay District (FHOD), and Smart Growth 
Overlay District (SGOD) for Smart Growth Overlay Plan Review and Coastal 
Resilience Overlay Site Plan Review in accordance with the following sections of the 
Salem Zoning Ordinance: Section 7.4 Smart Growth Overlay District and Section 8.9 
Coastal Resiliency Overlay District. Specifically, the applicant proposes the 
demolition of the buildings at 24 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 595) and 56 Margin 
Street (Map 25, Lot 597), the adaptive reuse of 54 Margin Street (Map 25, Lot 597), 
and the preservation of the façade of 20 Endicott Street (Map 25, Lot 597) to 
accommodate for a 22,806 square foot building comprised of 53 affordable homes, a 
shelter with 70 beds, and supportive programing space along with other site 
improvements. Thirteen parking spaces are proposed on site. 
 
Ms. Eimert discloses that she has submitted an appearance of conflict of interest 
form with the Mayor’s Office given her connection to the development of the 40R 
zoning. and will not be voting on this project. 
 
Andrew DeFranza, Harborlight Homes and Stefano Basso, SV Architects,  are in 
attendance for the Applicant.  
 
Mr. DeFranza recaps the project overview. Mr. Basso runs through changes based on 
feedback. They have decreased the number of siding changes and matched the brick 
of the church as much as possible; streamlined the roofs and carried flat cornice line 
through. Incorporated a precast stone based and kept the storefront curtain wall. 
Eliminated sloped roofs on Endicott Street and incorporated more Italianate 
features. There has been discussion among the project team to have a pop of color 
on some sort of detail. Memorial Park area with bricks, bell, and benches; the bell is 
to be moved to front of the church.  
 
Public Comment 
 
Written Public Comment 
 
Joe Cultrera 
Prescott Street
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes July 23, 2026 
Page 3 of 13 
 
Know your rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. c. 30A § 18-25 and City Ordinance § 2-2028 
through § 2-2033. 
Compliments Mr. DeFranza on the new look of the building; it seems to fit the block 
better. Still concerned that it is wall to wall buildings and there is no space for clients 
to hang out. Concerned about people walking past that block when there is no place 
for anyone to hang out. Glad peaks are gone and that the color is better. Says that 
the neighborhood has never been consulted about the design of the project despite 
promises from previous ward councilors. Does not think the bell outside the church 
is the proper place for it; thinks it will be damaged.  
 
Steve Kapantais 
23 Wisteria Street 
Tells Mr. Rieder that there is a possible meeting violation regarding Ms. Eimert as 
having a conflict of interest and remaining in the room when the proper procedure is 
considered that the member recuses themselves and not be in the room, potentially 
influencing the decision. Asks that Chair Rieder report the violation to the Ethics 
Commission.  
 
Polly Wilbert 
7 Cedar Street  
Hopes the DRB will consider that the development is a “bridge site” between 
downtown and the post-fire residential neighborhood. The development must 
transition from the hard edges of downtown to the soft edges of the neighborhood. 
Favors gables to help with the transition and break-up the massing. Hopes people  
have looked at the designed standards for the 40R. Doesn’t like the box/panel 
construction design. Post fire construction is a detail and characteristic that should 
be respected.  
 
Mark Stevens 
69 Summer Street 
Submitted photos of what his view is of the property. He is concerned about the 
façade. What will Pratt Street look like? It looks like 2 windows so he will look at a 
wall of siding and there is no bump out on the rendering and there is no setback on 
the street. There is opportunity to put sidewalk in place. On 2nd floor floorplan, looks 
like a tree is being planted. Wonders what the HVAC will look like to him. What 
about lighting? Is the stairwell exiting on Pratt Street for emergency use only?  
 
Barbara Mann and Bob Femino 
29 Endicott 32 Endicott 
Wants to see the plan for 24 Endicott Street. Ms. Cunninham reminds that the public 
comment period is for comments, not discussion. Mr. Femino says they couldn’t see 
view from Endicott Street. Mr. Rieder asks for a clarification on plan or rendering. 
Mr. Basso says that there isn’t a rendering of Endicott Street. Ms. Mann clarifies that 
she only cared about peaks on Endicott Street. Still curious about HVAC condensers
City of Salem Planning Board 
Minutes July 23, 2026

and what they will look like on the roof, the garage, and the memorial yard. Why a 
13 car garage when there are available spaces at Riley Plaza. Mr. Femino agrees with 
Ms. Wilbert regarding the roof. Understands that some prefer the changes, but they 
[the neighborhood] were never brought to the table regarding what they would like 
to see. The height matters, gables take away sun and breeze. Eliminating the garage 
would preserve the memorial. Ms. Mann invites everyone to visit the site.  
 
Mr. Rieder re-welcomes Ms. Eimert and thanks her for recusing herself from voting 
on this project. Mr. Rieder says that it is typical for those who have a conflict of 
interest step away for that agenda item and he invites her to do so. Ms. Eimert 
removes herself from the meeting for the remainder of the discussion. 
 
Planning Board Comments 
 
Mr. Furey commends the revised version of the plan. He reminds everyone that 
there is a human face to homelessness, that Salem is a welcoming city of 
neighborhoods, and this whole complex is part of the neighborhood onto Riley 
Plaza. This new facility is a positive for the people.  
 
Ms. Sides commends the team for responding with vast improvements and is  
looking forward to seeing the other elevations.  
 
Mr. Rieder calls an audible and invites James Z. to speak as he was unable to join 
during the public comment period. 
 
James Zaviglia 
25 High Street 
Reiterates what others have said about the memorial park and the bell. The 
Italian Club was built by the people in the neighborhood. The memorial is 
important because of the names on the bricks. Appreciates that change happens 
but would like some of the past preserved.  
 
Ms. Tarbet agrees with Ms. Sides. Encourages the team to seek a complimentary 
brick rather than a brick match. Likes the introduction of color on the base and 
agrees with the public comment on the screening of the roof HVACs. Wonders if 
there is room to locate the bell and memorial closer to its original location and if the 
team could work with the community to do this.  
 
Mr. Rieder is familiar with the area. Echoes the need for renders of Endicott Street 
and Pratt Street. In the previous presentation the thirteen (13) parking spaces were 
stated for employees. Is there potential for parking in Riley Plaza? Echoes the issue 
with placing the bell in the front. The rendering makes the bell seem ill at ease; the
City of Salem Planning Board

tri-fold interpretative board is also an issue. In the last meeting, Chair Rieder 
commented on the removal of trees so that the Applicant could replace the soils and 
plant new species, does not think Honey Locust is a good choice for this area. Agrees 
with Mr. Cultrera on the lack of open space.  
 
Design Review Board Comments 
 
Mr. Perras thinks the project is moving in the right direction. He would like to see a 
true elevation, especially going up Endicott Street to see the context. This will allow 
the DRB to have a better contextual understanding. Wonders how far back the 
connector pieces between the brick massing can be pushed. Could they be pushed 
back to create green space? Does not love the pop of color idea. Does not love the 
big cornices at the top.  
 
Ms. Miller clarifies that the DRB has not seen the full presentation and she 
happened to attend the last Planning Board meeting. It is hard to assess design 
when they don’t know program and entries. The first rendering is better than the 
second. Feels that if you are a person who needs a place to live, you want it to look 
like a normal looking apartment. Interested in seeing a developed landscape plan. 
 
Mr. Rieder confirms with Ms. Cunningham that the project has not been referred to 
the DRB. 
 
Mr. Estes agrees that the project is moving in the right direction and there is a need 
for green space. There is a massive HVAC unit on the center block.  
 
Ms. Murray lives in the neighborhood and appreciates the work done from the 
original plans to now. Agrees with Ms. Tarbet on the brick.  
 
Mr. Durand agrees with previous comments. Prefers this massing. Recommends 
investigating brick matching sooner rather than later. Concerned with HVAC 
screening. Would like to see the Endicott Street elevation as well. Feels the bell at 
the front of the building will suffer from vandalism. Also does not like the white on 
the side.  
 
Mr. Rieder agrees with Mr. Perras on the pop of color. There is no tree in the traffic 
island [as shown on the rendering]. Doesn’t know how you can reduce parking to 
allow for more open space. Imperative to have a set of true elevations on at least 
the three (3) primary sides. Astonished that Mr. Furey has not recommended that 
Mr. DeFranza meet with the neighborhood. These neighborhood meetings reduce 
tensions in public meetings and reduce the fear of the unknown.

A. 8 Harrison Road (Map 31, Lot 327), 9 Harrison Road (Map 31, Lot 340), 262 Loring 
Ave (Map 31, Lot 1), and 266 Loring Ave (Map 31, Lot 341), Salem, MA   
Applicant: Joseph C. Correnti, Esq. f/b/o WinnDevelopment Companies, LLC   
Description: A continuance of a public hearing for all persons interested in the 
application of Joseph C. Correnti, Esq. f/b/o WinnDevelopment Companies, LLC for 
the property located at 8 Harrison Road (Map 31, Lot 327), 9 Harrison Road (Map 31, 
Lot 340), 262 Loring Ave (Map 31, Lot 1), and 266 Loring Ave (Map 31, Lot 341) in 
the R1 (Residential One Family), RC (Residential Conservation), SGO (Smart Growth 
Overlay District), ECOD (Entrance Corridor Overlay District), and C-ROD (Coastal 
Resiliency Overlay District) Zoning Districts for Smart Growth Overlay District Plan 
Review and C-ROD Site Plan Review in accordance with the following sections of the 
Salem Zoning Ordinance: Section 7.4 Smart Growth Overlay District, Section 8.9 
Coastal Resiliency Overlay District, and Section 37 of the Salem Code of Ordinances, 
Stormwater Management Permit. Specifically, the applicant proposes a total of up to 
145 dwelling units through the adaptive reuse of three (3) existing Salem State 
University South Campus buildings (Harrington, Academic, and Alumni buildings) and 
the construction of one (1) new four-story residential building along Harrison Road. 
No changes are proposed to the footprints of the existing buildings. Site 
improvements will also include approximately 159 off-street surface parking spots 
and a connective network of landscaped common areas and pedestrian paths. This 
project is the second phase of two-phase project known collectively as the Forest 
River Residences, to be located at 8 Harrison Road (Map 31, Lot 327), 9 Harrison 
Road (Map 31, Lot 340), 262 Loring Ave (Map 31, Lot 1), and 266 Loring Ave (Map 
31, Lot 341).

C. 440 Highland Avenue (Map 3, Lot 4)  
Applicant: Kinetic Design and Development f/b/o Walmart 
Description: A public hearing for all persons interested in the application of Kinetic 
Design & Development F/b/o Walmart located at 440 Highland Avenue (Map 3, Lot 4) in 
the Business Park Development District (BPD) and Entrance Corridor Overlay District 
(ECOD) for Site Plan Review and Business Park Development Special Permit in 
accordance with Section 9.5 Site Plan Review and Section 8.3 Business Park 
Development District of the Salem Zoning Ordinance. Specifically, the applicant 
proposes to internally renovate and repair the vacant storefronts in the plaza to move 
their “Spark” program Depot from the existing Walmart. No changes to the building 
footprint are proposed. 
 
Steve Martorano from Bohler is in attendance for the Applicant. Carla Hackett, Walmart, 
Griffen Bobbit and Kyle Gardiner, Kinetics, Bill Scully, Mckinely Horn. 
 
Mr. Martorano shares his screen and explains what the Depot program is: online orders 
and is what you would get in a neighborhood market but no customers shopping. The 
project is in front of the Board as the space is over ten thousand (10000) square feet. As 
the project is gig driver oriented, there is no real increase in traffic. 
 
The team did a light level survey; there are no improvements needed.  
 
A comprehensive traffic study was completed. There is already a similar type of delivery 
system operating out of the Walmart. Those drivers will shift to the new Depot facility; 
there will be modest increase in traffic to the site, and more traffic would be associated 
if the site reverted to traditional retail. 
 
Public Comment 
 
None 
 
Planning Board Comments 
 
Mr. Furey Walmart has been a major asset to Salem.  
 
Ms. Eimert asks if they have spoken to the Zoning Enforcement Officer for the Site Plan 
Review (SPR)? Mr. Martorano says that they received comments that as the space is

and he has the same question. Ms. Eimert asks that there be documentation from the 
Zoning Enforcement Officer on the use proposed and the jurisdiction of the Planning 
Board regarding the requirements of site plan review with regards to the entrance 
corridor overlay zoning to bring it into compliance under that special permit and site
